author: EmuCore - Hub
title: I Wish I Grew Up With the PlayStation 2.
summary: bubbletea approaches the PS2 catalogue without childhood nostalgia, spending thirty-eight minutes across platformers, JRPGs, action games and oddities to ask what the generation means to someone discovering it later.

blocks.text: The essay reverses the usual retrospective premise: the creator did not grow up with PS2 and therefore cannot use personal memory as the main recommendation. Ratchet, Jak and Sly establish the platformer lineage; Final Fantasy X, Dragon Quest VIII and Persona 3 open different JRPG traditions; Kingdom Hearts, Devil May Cry, Katamari, Ape Escape 2 and Chulip widen the tone. The chapter structure lets a modern first-time player explain which design languages remain inviting and which expectations came from later games.

This is a curated personal encounter, not a representative sample of thousands of releases. Several highlighted series are famous precisely because later discussion kept them visible, while sports, racing, licensed games, regional exclusives and many experimental titles receive little or no space. The creator’s lack of childhood attachment reduces one bias but introduces present-day taste, ports and retrospective reputation. Use the essay to compare discovery with memory, then explore less canonized software before generalizing about what the PS2 generation “was.”
